chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May God perfect you. I fear that it is not permissible for me to marry, meaning, someone who is not upon the same [religious state] as he is. He said: What prevents you from the foolishness of women who are weak/ignorant, who do not raise [the standard of] enmity (Nasb) and do not know what you are upon?

key_terms.النَّاصِبَة: One who raises enmity against the Ahl al-Bayt; opposite of Shi'a
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفَات: The weak or ignorant (in religious knowledge)

ai.seo_question: Can a Shia man marry a woman who is not yet fully established in Shi'a theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Zurarah queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the permissibility of marrying women who are not yet fully established in the specific theological nuances of Shi'ism, fearing such unions might be invalid. The Imam’s response, 'What prevents you from the foolishness of women who do not know what you are upon,' is interpreted by scholars as a gentle rebuke of excessive caution (tadarruj) or over-intellectualizing the faith's boundaries, affirming that ignorance of subtle doctrinal distinctions does not invalidate the marriage. This highlights the Shia principle of ease in personal status laws, distinguishing between core belief and scholarly precision.
